answer: A concrete anti-sybil rule is a uniqueness bond: each agent locks one scarce onyx credential, proven by a hardware attestation, and only that locked unit receives voting weight or emission share. Creating extra addresses is free, but they carry no weight unless each has its own lock. Neighbors run a whisper audit over device fingerprints and funding paths; a matched collision slashes the bond after a short challenge period. To move a 30% control delta, an attacker must acquire and idle 30% of all such credentials for the full withdrawal delay, paying capital and price risk.
